001.summary: Game one of four at Alex's, three-player. The pilot mulliganed into a hand he calls "structurally dead": a clean land base, one-drop instants and sorceries, Crimson Wisps and Storm-Kiln Artist, and zero goblins — the whole storm-and-copy half in hand with nothing to multiply through. He files it as a bad draw and a bad keep rather than a deck problem and made no changes; the entry's decklist_sha256 matches the current list, so the 99 is unchanged since.

cards.why: in the opening hand and inert: the note says he "had the entire storm-and-copy half of the engine in hand and nothing to multiply through".
same hand, same reason — a copy engine "with no body to target is a hand that does nothing, however good the individual cards look".

decisions.spot: the game-one mulligan: a clean land base, one-drop instants and sorceries, Crimson Wisps and Storm-Kiln Artist, and zero goblins — keep or ship

takeaways: The mulligan gate for this deck is GOBLIN PRESENCE, not cantrip density — the pilot's own words.
A hand of cantrips plus a copy engine with no body to target does nothing however good the individual cards look; the pilot's verdict is that he should have shipped it.
No deck change follows from this game: the pilot reads it as a bad draw and a bad keep, and the list stays pinned at v1.0.0, precon as printed.

open_questions.question: After mulligans, how often does this 99 present an opening hand with at least one cheap goblin body — the gate the pilot says he should be mulliganing to?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot has named goblin presence as his keep criterion but has no figure for how often the deck can meet it, so he cannot know whether the gate is a reasonable one to hold or one that would ship too many hands.

002.summary: Game one of three at Oliver's, five-player. The pilot kept three basics, a utility land and Krenko, Mob Boss — "land and a value engine and NO SMALL GOBLINS" — and with the instants and sorceries all expensive the cantrip half never turned over and the engine never assembled. The table was three mono-red decks and Oliver killed it on turn five off Krenko tokens and pings. This is the second logged game lost to the same keep criterion.

opponents.evidence: Tom on Purphoros doing the same
five-player pod: Sean, Oliver, Tom, Alex, Ryan

cards.why: kept as the hand's value engine; the note says the hand had "land and a value engine and NO SMALL GOBLINS", and "the engine never assembled".

decisions.spot: the opener at Oliver's: three basics, a utility land and Krenko, Mob Boss, with no cheap goblins — keep or mulligan (the same decision as entry 001, on a different hand)

takeaways: The pilot restates the same gate he named in entry 001: GOBLIN PRESENCE gates the mulligan, not cantrip density, and cheap goblin bodies are non-negotiable for the deck to function.
In this game the instants and sorceries in hand were all expensive, so the cantrip half never turned over — the fuel stage failed alongside the body pile, not instead of it.
The pod itself was a factor the pilot names: three mono-red decks, and the red density took the game over before his own engine came online.

open_questions.question: Does the 99 carry enough cheap goblin bodies, and cheap enough instants and sorceries, to support the keep criterion the pilot has now stated twice — or is the gate unmeetable as the list is built?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both logged games are losses with the same shape: a hand the pilot liked, no small goblins, engine never assembled. Two games is thin, but it is the same failure twice and the pilot has twice declined to change the deck over it, so the doctor should say whether the keep rule or the list is the thing that has to move.

003.summary: A win at Ryan's (the note's game 2) against Alex's R/G fight deck and Ryan's T'Vol. Sean used Deflecting Swat to save Zada from Alex's fight and Untimely Malfunction to break Ryan's Phyrexian Altar engine. Alex then killed Ryan. Per the pilot's own correction, Empty the Warrens with Impact Tremors came the turn before; the kill turn was 15 goblins and about 15 mana, Reckless Ransacking plus the three haste-and-draw spells (Accelerate, Crimson Wisps, Expedite) and a swing with 20-plus trample goblins at Alex. The game was played on an earlier list (V4, v1.2.0). V5 changed one card (Faithless Looting out, Goblin Sharpshooter in), and that card is not named in the note. The body says +3/+2 and the correction says +4/+2. Both are left as written.

takeaways: Sequencing and having the right answer at the right time won it: Deflecting Swat kept the commander and Untimely Malfunction broke the table's engine.
Removing the engine piece the whole game turns on is right even when it is called kingmaking. Sean's reasoning was that without it the game was over.
The pilot's follow-up is none: "The bracket 3 tune is working."

open_questions.question: On the kill turn, which card gave the goblins trample? Reckless Ransacking's oracle is +3/+2 and a Treasure, and the note gives the final pump as both +3/+2 and +4/+2.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This was the deck's best turn on record. Lifting it as a stack would make it a cited win line rather than a recollection.

004.summary: Game 1 at Oliver's against an optimized bracket-3 table. Tom went turn-one Sol Ring into a turn-two Purphoros, the game was effectively over by turn four, and Sean never cast Zada. The pilot says he should have mulliganed. He reads the loss as a tier mismatch, not a deck defect: the clock is one to two turns too slow for this table. He names two levers for a future branch (wide before Zada, or Zada faster) and says "do not iterate now". The list is the current one.

opponents.evidence: Oliver: Balin (token maker; Krenko in game 3)

cards.why: "Krenko is in the list and almost never shows up. Sample size is small — more at-bats before drawing conclusions."

decisions.spot: the game-one opening hand against a table aiming to win around turn four: keep or ship (the hand itself is not recorded)

takeaways: This deck cannot beat a turn-two Purphoros without early interaction. The counterplay comes earlier: deny the Sol Ring.

Mulligan heuristic (proposed): keep a hand that either makes many goblin tokens before Zada, or lands Zada fast with a payoff to accelerate off her. Ship hands with neither, including good-land, cantrip-heavy hands. This is the third logged game, after 001 and 002, where the keep is the lesson.
Against the Oliver/Tom table the clock is one to two turns too slow. Against the B team the deck is "great, fun". This is a tier mismatch, not a deck defect, and the deck is not to be iterated now.

open_questions.question: Which lever buys back the one to two turns: wide before Zada (more token makers and cheap goblins) or Zada faster (more rocks, dorks or treasure for a turn-two or turn-three Zada)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot says to "pick one direction" for the future feature branch, and the two levers want different slots.

open_questions.question: How often does the current 99 present an opener that meets the proposed keep rule: many goblin tokens before Zada, or Zada on turn two or three with a payoff?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without a figure, the pilot cannot tell whether the rule is one he can hold or one that ships too many hands. The note also flags "possibly also a draw/consistency problem — flag for measurement rather than assume".

open_questions.question: The note says "Enchantment removal should be a standing slot audit across decks." What does this 99 run that answers a resolved enchantment?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Purphoros is an enchantment, and both losses that night ran through it.

005.summary: Game 2 at Oliver's, a rematch with the same decks. Sean removed Tom's Sol Ring with Abrade, which delayed Purphoros but did not stop it. He assembled the engine (Zada, Storm-Kiln Artist, a pile of treasure and one of the new card-draw spells), but took roughly 10 then 12 ping damage per cycle plus constant attacks. The small goblins he needed to copy spells kept dying, and he lost on the clock. The pilot's read: "Engine assembly worked. Survival did not." The list is the current one.

opponents.evidence: Tom opened Sol Ring again. Sean removed it with Abrade
Oliver ran his Balin token line
Sean and Ryan middled with thin boards

cards.why: removed Tom's turn-one Sol Ring: "the single most impactful play of the night"; "Abrade came in exactly when needed".
part of the engine that assembled; "Engine assembly worked. Survival did not."

decisions.spot: turn one against Tom's Sol Ring: Abrade it now, accepting the salt, or develop

takeaways: Deny the Sol Ring opener. Early artifact removal is a legitimate tempo play against this pod: expect salt, do it anyway.
Assembling the engine is not winning. Once Purphoros resolved, the deck had no way to stop the ping damage, and the small goblins the copy plan needs were the first to die.
Threat removal beats tempo: when the whole table names the threat and only you can answer it, answer it.
The new card-draw additions helped, and artifact removal in red is worth the slot.

open_questions.question: Once Purphoros resolves on the other side, does this 99 have any card that removes it or stops its damage, or does the deck have to race?
open_questions.why_it_matters: "The deck had no way to stop the ping damage once Purphoros resolved." Purphoros is on the pilot's kill-on-sight list and decided both games that night.

open_questions.question: With about 2 damage per small goblin per cycle killing the copy bodies, how many turns does the engine get between assembly and death at the 10-12 per cycle the note records?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This tells apart "too slow by a turn" from "cannot win through a resolved Purphoros at all", and the two point at different branches.
